assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Z2 topological-insulator classification and the quantum spin Hall effect reorganised how band structures are understood: a topological invariant of the electronic structure that protects edge states, with experimental realisation in HgTe wells and a very large downstream literature in materials, spintronics and topological quantum matter. As an electronic-structure theorist I regard this as a conceptual change in what band theory can say, not just a new material.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical prediction and the Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group delivered the decisive quantum spin Hall measurement in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. This gives a clean three-person theory-plus-experiment configuration. Hasan's ARPES work on three-dimensional topological insulators is real and important, and the supplied credit omits other key theorists, so the allocation between the 2D and 3D parts is not fully resolved.
assessment.maturity: Close to two decades of independent confirmation across many material families, with robust interpretation and a stable framework. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Some principal contributors to the HgTe proposal and to the 3D extension are not in the credited names, and I cannot verify how the credit boundary would be drawn.
Whether the 3D topological insulator experiments should be recognised alongside the 2D quantum spin Hall work is unresolved.
Recollection of detailed priority claims is from memory and not independently checked.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the exact limit of infinite dimensions turned into a practical non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, and combined with DFT (LDA+DMFT) it is a working tool for real correlated materials such as Mott systems, transition-metal oxides and f-electron compounds. It explained the Mott transition and spectral weight transfer in a quantitatively useful way and is used daily in my own field.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensions limit; Georges and Kotliar built the DMFT mapping to the impurity problem and later the material-specific implementation. The supplied names cover the central trio, but Metzner is not included, and the contribution of Kotliar's group to the DFT combination is distinct from the original formulation, so credit allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of development, validated against spectroscopy and transport experiments, and now embedded in widely used codes. Mature, with ongoing debate about the accuracy of the impurity solvers and systematic corrections beyond single-site DMFT.
uncertainties: Metzner's role is not represented in the credited names, which weakens a clean attribution.
Because this is a computational and theoretical method, an award would require a clear argument about discovery versus tool; my own closeness to the field may bias me upward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted flat bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene, and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018 opened moiré engineering as a new platform for correlated and topological matter. Graphene itself demonstrated that stability of two-dimensional crystals overturned earlier expectations; twist control adds a tunable correlated-electron laboratory of broad impact.
assessment.attribution: MacDonald with Bistritzer made the decisive theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive experiments with Cao et al. Two laureates form the most natural pairing. Adding Bistritzer is possible but I treat his contribution as joint with MacDonald, and other experimental and theoretical contributors (for example the Dean and Young groups and earlier theory by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto) complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Seven to eight years of intense independent replication with a very strong body of follow-up work, though the nature of the superconducting state remains debated. Moderately early, but the discovery itself is well confirmed.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in twisted graphene is unsettled.
Earlier theoretical work on twisted-bilayer band structure may dilute exclusive credit to the Bistritzer-MacDonald model.
Timing may be premature compared with candidates that have longer track records.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The defect-mediated melting theory and the hexatic phase are a classic of statistical physics: two-dimensional melting by two successive continuous transitions driven by dislocation and disclination unbinding, with universal predictions confirmed in colloidal and other two-dimensional systems. It extended the 2016 recognition of topological phase transitions into the crystalline setting and links to my interest in materials with reduced dimensionality.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson formulated the theory and Young computed the critical behaviour, with Kosterlitz and Thouless as the conceptual root already recognised in 2016. A three-person configuration of Halperin, Nelson and Young is internally coherent, though the share of Kosterlitz-Thouless-adjacent priority is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Theory from the late 1970s with decades of experimental and simulation confirmation, including colloid experiments; some details of whether melting is first order or two-step in particular systems remain system-dependent. Long mature, so there is no timing risk beyond being a late recognition.
uncertainties: Recognition could appear partially redundant with the 2016 prize.
Evidence for the hexatic phase is system-dependent and in some systems first-order melting competes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and the giant TMR in MgO-barrier junctions made spin-dependent tunnelling a technology basis for hard-disk read heads and magnetic random access memory. The physics rests on spin-polarised tunnelling and coherent symmetry-filtered transport, which is a natural complement to the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance and sits close to my own magnetism field.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki independently observed room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin and Yuasa/Djayaprawira groups realised giant TMR in MgO junctions in 2004, following theoretical predictions by Butler and Mathon-Umerski that are not among the credited names. The supplied three names can support a fair prize, but the theoretical predictions and the Yuasa contribution complicate the claim.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation and large-scale commercialisation. Well matured and stable.
uncertainties: The prediction of symmetry filtering by Butler et al. and Mathon-Umerski is outside the credited names.
The relative priority of Moodera versus Miyazaki and the Yuasa/Parkin MgO contributions is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard-type model Hamiltonians with tunable parameters, including the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and fermionic Hubbard physics, giving a quantum simulator for strongly correlated matter. It gives direct experimental access to many-body questions that my own computational field attacks with approximations.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition; Esslinger's group extended this to fermions and Fermi-Hubbard physics. With five credited names, choosing three requires dropping either Greiner or Cirac; I pick Bloch, Zoller and Esslinger as a theory-experiment configuration, aware that Greiner's contribution to the Mott insulator observation is substantial.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of development with independent groups worldwide; quantum gas microscopes and fermionic simulation have matured, though the physical regime of the hardest Hubbard problems (d-wave superconductivity) is not yet reached.
uncertainties: Adjacent AMO recognition in 1997, 2001 and 2012 may reduce appetite for another cold-atom prize.
Whether the simulator has yet resolved an open question in correlated matter is unsettled.
Omitting Greiner and Cirac is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmion lattices in chiral magnets, with emergent electrodynamics, topological Hall effect and ultralow-current-density manipulation, are a clear example of topology entering magnetism, with a link to spintronic concepts and memory proposals. The connection to micromagnetic and atomistic spin simulations of noncollinear order is directly in my area.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit is limited to Pfleiderer and Tokura. The theoretical prediction by Bogdanov and Rossler and the first observation by Muhlbauer et al. in MnSi (Pfleiderer's group) and the real-space imaging in FeCoSi by Yu et al. (Tokura's group) are the experimental pillars. Because the credited names omit Bogdanov, an allocation including the theoretical prediction is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years since the MnSi observation with extensive independent confirmation; the application side (racetrack memory) is not yet realised, which tempers the case for technological impact but not for scientific discovery.
uncertainties: The credited names omit the theoretical prediction (Bogdanov and collaborators), so a fair configuration may not be possible from the supplied credit.
Practical device impact remains unproven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third class of collinear magnetic order with compensated moments yet spin-split bands from crystal symmetry, supported by spin-group classification and ab initio calculations. The idea is conceptually clean and relevant to spintronics, and it is the kind of result that DFT-based analysis supports directly, including ARPES and magnetic-circular-dichroism evidence in candidate materials such as MnTe and CrSb.
assessment.attribution: The credited trio is plausible as the group that articulated the classification and its consequences, but several parallel contributions (Hayami, Yanagi and Kusunose; Yuan and Zunger; the Sinova-Jungwirth anomalous Hall work on RuO2 and the experimental teams) and the ongoing materials debate make attribution unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Premature relative to other candidates: the concept dates to about 2019-2022 and RuO2 in particular became contested. Confirmation in MnTe and CrSb is encouraging but young.
uncertainties: Independent confirmation is still accumulating and the status of the flagship RuO2 candidate is disputed.
Priority among several groups proposing related symmetry-based spin splitting is not settled.
Technological relevance is at the proposal stage.
